problemStatement.formal: Formalize structural obstacles to a short Kempe-chain proof of the four color theorem, including free-color pigeonhole facts, chain interference, and reducibility-style minimum-counterexample checks.
problemStatement.plain: Backfills metadata for the Four Color Theorem OQ-01 investigation. The Lean file proves small graph-coloring and Kempe-chain obstruction lemmas explaining why the five-color Kempe strategy does not directly yield a human-readable four-color proof.
whyMatters: The four color theorem is historically important precisely because the accepted proof is computer-assisted.
Kempe-chain failures explain why a tempting human-scale proof strategy breaks down.
The metadata surfaces the proved obstruction lemmas while keeping the full four-color theorem's axiom-backed status separate.

proven: `free_color_of_degree_lt` proves the pigeonhole free-color principle for graph coloring.
`five_color_degree_four` records the degree-four extension step behind five-color-style arguments.
`degree_five_all_colors_possible` and `four_color_degree_five_pigeonhole` capture the degree-five bottleneck for four colors.
`min_counterexample_has_low_degree` and `config_reduction` record minimum-counterexample and reducibility-style checks.
`FourColorTheoremOQ01.lean` is recorded with 0 axioms and 0 sorries, while the base four-color theorem file remains axiom-backed.
open: A genuinely human-readable proof of the full four color theorem remains outside this file.
The complete computer-assisted reducible-configuration verification is not formalized here.
knownResults.goal: Expose the theorem-backed Kempe-chain obstruction and coloring-structure metadata without overstating the full four-color theorem.

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: Created FourColorTheoremOQ01.lean with 0 axioms, 0 sorries. Formalized the Kempe chain interference obstruction (why 5-color Kempe works but 4-color fails), free color pigeonhole theorem, Heawood counterexample structure, and minimum counterexample analysis.

free_color_of_degree_lt: pigeonhole principle for graph coloring
chain_interference_obstruction: algebraic proof that two chains on shared vertex interfere
five_color_no_double_swap: C(5,2) > C(4,2) showing 5 colors have more freedom
Gallery entry: four-color-theorem-oq-01 with full meta.json, index.ts, annotations.json
insights: Degree < k colors guarantees free color by pigeonhole - no chain swaps needed
5-color case: ONE Kempe swap suffices, planarity prevents interference
4-color case: TWO swaps needed, chains can share vertices causing interference
C(5,2)=10 vs C(4,2)=6 color pairs - more pairs give more degrees of freedom
Heawood 1890: constructed specific graph where both chains connect, forced to cross by planarity
No human-readable 4CT proof known as of 2025; alternative approaches (flow, algebraic) incomplete
